root_cause_label: Agent abandoned mandatory UPC/upcc requirement when environment obstacle (slow UPC build) was encountered, substituting pthreads+gcc instead and never producing a UPC-based parallel executable
one_sentence_failure_summary: Faced with a slow UPC compiler installation, the agent abandoned the explicit UPC requirement and implemented a pthreads-based parallel version that also produced incorrect output, failing on both the technology spec and output correctness.
t_err_evidence: Step 8: Agent writes pgen_pthreads.c, explicitly stating 'Instead of compiling Berkeley UPC from source, I'll focus on creating a simpler parallel implementation using pthreads directly, which doesn't require the UPC compiler.' This is the decisive choice to violate the UPC requirement.
t_commit_evidence: Step 9: Agent renames pgen_pthreads.c to pgen.c and rewrites the Makefile to use gcc -pthread instead of upcc, fully committing to a non-UPC parallel build system with no path back to UPC.
t_surface_evidence: Step 18: Automated diff comparison first shows 'CONTIGS DIFFER', providing an observable failure signal that the parallel output does not match the serial output.
trigger_explanation: The Berkeley UPC compiler build was slow/timing out (a real environment obstacle). Rather than persisting with UPC installation (e.g., waiting longer, trying a prebuilt binary, or using a network-based UPC translator), the agent wrongly concluded UPC was unavailable and substituted pthreads, discarding the explicit task requirement to use UPC compiled with upcc and run via upcrun.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 5-7: Repeated UPC configure/build attempts produce very long configure output but no completed build; step 6 shows apt search finds no UPC package; step 7 re-attempts configure with additional disable flags. These are warning signals that the UPC installation path is problematic, preceding the commit to abandon it at step 9.
